questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good location, not too far from Denmark, and has a good law program. I wanted to go somewhere I haven't been before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the University provided us with e-mails through each step.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of information through e-mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were two campuses to choose from. Not a lot of options, so you have to be quick if you want to live there.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: On campus, there was a big shared kitchen with cooking facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You don't/can't get a single room even if you apply for one on your application and they give you the option to choose. All Erasmus students are offered shared double rooms only. Bring your own kitchen utensils or buy some when you arrive. There are lots of parties on campus and it is big. I lived on Campus Martinitt which is one of the good ones, but it is placed outside of the city and in a bad neighborhood. Very good public transportation from there anyways. Bus stop right in front of the building that goes directly to the city center of Milan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You received e-mails for every step so it was simple and easy. Just stay updated and check your mails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office was always available. They reply to e-mails very quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and even changed my mind a couple of times throughout the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it. There isn't really a deadline, they are not strict at all. You can try as many courses as you want and change before you make a decision.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were okay, but the level was not as high as we are used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, basically only lectures and discussion based. Your grade depends on how active you are during the course as well. No group work, some presentations, but pretty much only lectures in classrooms.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Law, Culture & Development in a global world
Smart cities, artificial intelligence, and digital transformation law
Trade liberalization & labour rights 
Comparative labour law 
European Monetary and Economic law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend "Comparative Labour Law" because it was interesting and relevant but mostly because of Professor Biasi. He was so nice and entertaining and not like other teachers. It was a comfortable course with a multiple-choice exam. I also recommend "Smart Cities" if you want an easy course, because it did not require anything and the exam was very easy. Not a lot of study material either.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any. You have to buy a router for internet if you live on campus, but I didn't have to because I lived in the main building were it worked.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than I expected. Public transportation was very cheap. You can get a monthly travel card for students for only 22 euros per month. Eating and drinking out was not as expensive as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really anything that I know of at my University. But ESN was a very good organization for exchange students!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend traveling as much as you can. Milan is close to everything, so take the train and go on day trips and weekend trips! I also recommend becoming a member of ESN and joining their activities. They arrange trips and parties, eating out ect.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips! Visit all the Italian cities you can around Milan. I went to Switzerland and France as well by train, so easy!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took a couple of weeks. It was not super easy but once you get used to it, it's very fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, join ESN. You will meet so many exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Italians are very laid back, so even University and exams are quite informal. It was surprising how you could have an oral exam in a room with other people. 
It was also difficult to communicate sometimes, as most Italians aren't good at speaking English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated how open and friendly Italians are. The food was amazing!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Travel as much as you can
Don't focus too much on school, it is not hard to pass
Try to learn Italian

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to attend the Italian language course that is offered.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the traveling and meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the culture and learning Italian.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
